title: Contract tranche apportionment map — FY29 (working sheet)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working allocation sheet for Dedicated contract tranches for FY29. The goal is to map each contract tranche to region and GPU pool, show provisional slices, flag exposed run-rate risk, and list short-term operational actions (swapbacks, backfills, emergency foam).

Notes (high level):
- This is intentionally granular (per-tranche) because many corporate contracts require month-by-month apportionment and cross-region fallbacks.
- Key terms: tranche = a contract-specified portion of a customer commitment (often monthly or quarterly).
- We keep a 10–20% operational buffer for burst and repair windows; column "buffer_pct" below is the recommended soft buffer.
- Backfill policy: when a tranche is underutilized for 2 consecutive weeks, we can backfill with pooled burst for best-effort customers. See JIRA-INFRA-1428 for approval thresholds.
- Swapback: temporary reassigning of GPUs between tranches (requires approval for >48h).

Legend / column defs:
- Contract: short customer label
- Tranche ID: internal tranche code (contract-month)
- Model Pool: H100-80GB | A100-80GB | L40 | T4 (legacy)
- Region: us-west-2 | eu-west-1 | asia-southeast-1
- Reserved GPUs: integer Gpu count reserved for tranche
- Reserved hours/month: Reserved GPUs * 24 * days_in_month (shows provisioning capacity)
- Expected utilization %: historical run-rate estimate (0–100)
- Effective used GPUs (est): Reserved GPUs * Expected utilization %
- Buffer %: recommended buffer on top of committed to cover burst/repairs
- Soft-alloc (GPUs): Reserved GPUs + ceil(Reserved GPUs * Buffer %)
- Commitment window: start — end
- Notes/constraints: short text

--- derived summary rows ---
Total reserved GPUs (active tranches): 132
Weighted avg expected utilization: 0.74
Total soft-alloc GPUs (with buffers): 150
Operational buffer (soft-alloc - reserved): 18 GPUs (~13.6% of reserved)
Projected exposed run-rate (if all tranches hit expected): approx 110 effective GPUs used vs 150 alloc => 26% spare available for best-effort allocations

Open assumptions / questions:
- Days_in_month used for Reserved hrs/mo calculation set to 30 in this sheet; adjust for month-specific runbooks when converting to billing exports.
- We assumed heterogeneous rack compatibility (H100 and A100 pools co-locate); some customers require physical isolation (see FinServe).
- Network egress limits per region not modeled here — check with networking team before cross-region swapbacks.

Short-term ops actions (next 30d):
- [ ] Approve backfill threshold policy (proposal in JIRA-INFRA-1428) — owner: Carlos Rivera — due 2029-01-22
- [ ] Validate FinServe private overlay schedule with solutions eng — owner: Lena Zhang — due 2029-01-30
- [ ] Run swapback dry-run for AcmeAI -> MarketLab (2 GPUs for 48h) — owner: Omar Haddad — due 2029-01-20
- [ ] Add per-month day-counts to reserved hrs export and recalc billing exposure — owner: Maya Patel — due 2029-01-18

Risk register (short):
- Late delivery of private overlay for FinServe -> high SLA exposure; mitigation: temporary isolation via dedicated sub-pool (requires manual ops).
- Unplanned MarketLab increase -> run-rate exposure in Q3; mitigation: pre-approved emergency ad-hoc slice (8 GPUs) gated by finance signoff.
- Region-specific hardware failure (eu-west-1) -> 10–15% capacity hit for EU tranches; mitigation: cross-region spillover policy to us-west-2 limited by egress rules.

Historical notes (why this sheet exists):
- Derived from customer conversations in Dec 2028 where several contracts requested explicit monthly tranche maps.
- Consolidates ask from sales (contract specifics) and SRE (placement constraints).

Version notes / changelog (short):
- 2028-11-02: initial draft created (Maya)
- 2028-12-10: added MarketLab Q4 projection and buffer calc (Carlos)
- 2029-01-08: updated FinServe dates after legal review (Lena)
- 2029-01-15: current — review and approval pass started

Appendix: quick calc examples
- Soft-alloc GPUs = Reserved GPUs + ceil(Reserved GPUs * Buffer %) -> used to size physical racks and predict logical slot exhaustion.
- Effective used GPUs = Reserved GPUs * Expected util % -> used to estimate run-rate consumption for autoscaling triggers.

Questions for reviewers:
- Is 10–15% buffer acceptable across all model pools or should L40 pools get a higher buffer due to repair frequency?
- Do we want to enforce region affinity hard constraints for retail customers?

References and links (in-text):
- Capacity runbook: confluence://capacity-runbook/fy29-apportionment
- Swapback policy draft: JIRA-INFRA-1428
- Dedicated contract template: confluence://templates/dedicated-contracts

(End of sheet — this remains a working document; please comment inline in Drive rather than creating separate copies.)
